title: Text tracks of lazy-loading media elements are fetched before the media resumes
body:
The [track processing model](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#start-the-track-processing-model) starts as soon as the `track` element is inserted into a media element:

> When a text track corresponding to a `track` element experiences any of the following circumstances, the user agent must start the `track` processing model for that text track and its `track` element:
>
> * The `track` element is created.
> * The text track has its text track mode changed.
> * The `track` element's parent element changes and the new parent is a media element.

...and nothing in it looks at the media element's [lazy loading attribute](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#lazy-loading-attribute), so for `<video loading=lazy src=...><track src=... default>` below the viewport, the text track is fetched immediately even though the media resource is deferred.

In Chrome Canary, the track fetch appears to be deferred along with the media: the `track` element's `readyState` stays `NONE` while the video is deferred, with the track's `mode` at `"showing"`, and the track loads once the video resumes.

Deferring seems like the better behavior, since the point of `loading=lazy` is to avoid fetching for offscreen media. Maybe the processing model should return early while the parent media element's load is deferred, with the media element's [lazy load resumption steps](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#lazy-load-resumption-steps) restarting it for each `track` child?

No wpt covers this either way.

(Found while investigating #12973.)
